chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Let the man spend with moderation and sufficiency, and he should forward the surplus from it for his Hereafter, for that is more lasting for the bounties, and closer to the increase from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and more beneficial regarding good health.'
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim balance spending and saving for the Hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) links financial moderation (qasd) directly to the preservation of divine favor (baqa' al-ni'ma), a concept central to Shia ethical theology. By allocating surplus wealth for the Hereafter, one not only secures spiritual reward but also ensures physical health and sustenance, reflecting the holistic Shia view of material and spiritual well-being. This teaching underscores the principle that moderation is not mere austerity, but a strategic stewardship of Allah's trust.
